answer: Like a zephyr that cannot fake its path across a reef, or a comet that burns fuel to return, a sybil farm must pay per-node energy and stake that honest single agents never do, making mass fakery economically irrational. Each agent must stake a bond locked to a unique hardware root and pass periodic proof-of-work challenges whose difficulty scales with fleet size, so spinning up many identities multiplies real compute cost. In practice, Agent0046 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
